energy: the ability to make something happen or change
heat: energy that makes things warm
fuel: something that stores energy to be burned, like petrol or coal
stored energy: energy held ready, as in food, a battery, or a lifted stone
renewable: energy that will not run out, like sun, wind and water
change of form: energy turning from one kind into another

chapters.title: The Word for Everything That Happens

pages.text: Nothing in the world happens without energy. A ball only rolls, a fire only burns, a heart only beats, because energy is at work. Energy is what makes things move, grow, glow and change. It is one of the biggest ideas in all of science, and once you see it, you start to see it everywhere.

image.note: A single frame full of action: a kicked ball, a cooking pot, a running child, a bright lamp

pages.text: You cannot hold energy in your hand like a stone. It is not a thing so much as an ability, the ability to make something happen. But it is completely real. You feel it when the sun warms your skin, when a hot meal fills you, and when your own tired legs finally run out of it near the end of a long day.

image.note: A child slowing to a stop at the end of a race, tired; the idea of "running out" of energy

pages.text: Energy comes in many forms. The easiest to see is the energy of movement. Anything that moves, a rolling ball, a running child, a gust of wind, a flowing river, carries energy simply because it is moving. The faster and heavier it is, the more of this moving energy it holds.

image.note: A river, a runner, and wind in trees, each drawn with motion lines; movement as energy

pages.text: Heat is energy too, and so is light, and so is sound. When you cook food, you pour heat energy into it. When a lamp glows, energy is leaving it as light. When a drum booms, energy is leaving it as sound. All these different things are really one thing wearing different clothes.

image.note: A pot of energy shown turning into heat, light, sound in three arrows; unified idea

pages.text: But energy does not have to be moving. It can be stored, sitting quietly, ready to act. Pull back a catapult and hold it still, and it is packed with stored energy, waiting to fling. Lift a stone high and hold it, and gravity has loaded it with stored energy, waiting to fall. Stillness can hide great power.

image.note: A stretched catapult held taut, and a stone held high; both drawn with a faint glow of stored energy

pages.text: The most useful stored energy of all is hidden inside food and fuel. A bowl of rice, a lump of coal, a tank of petrol, all hold energy locked up in them, waiting to be set free. Your body unlocks the energy in food. An engine unlocks the energy in fuel. Storing energy is how we keep power ready for when we need it.

image.note: A plate of jollof rice, a fuel can, and a battery side by side, each glowing gently inside; stored energy

chapters.title: The Great Rule: It Never Vanishes

pages.text: Now for the single most important rule about energy, one that has never once been broken. Energy is never made from nothing, and it never truly disappears. It only ever changes from one form into another. When energy seems to vanish, it has really just turned into a form you were not watching for.

image.note: A loop of arrows showing energy changing form and coming back round; nothing lost

pages.text: Watch it happen. You eat rice, and its stored energy becomes the moving energy of your running legs, and some becomes heat, which is why you grow warm as you run. Not one scrap was lost. It simply changed clothes, from food, to movement, to heat. This happens in everything, always.

image.note: A child eating then running and glowing warm; arrows tracing food energy to motion to heat

pages.text: Trace almost any energy back far enough and you reach the same place: the Sun. Sunlight grows the plants. The plants feed the animals and us. Plants that died long ago turned slowly into coal and oil deep underground. So the petrol in a car is really ancient sunlight, stored for millions of years and burned in a moment.

image.note: A chain: Sun to plant to buried plant to coal to car; ancient sunlight made visible

pages.text: Even the wind and the rivers we use for power are driven by the Sun, which stirs the air and lifts the water into the sky. Almost every fire, every meal, every gust and every wave traces back to that one great store of energy pouring down on us every single day. We are, nearly all of us, living on sunlight.

image.note: The Sun above, with wind, rain, rivers and growing crops all flowing from it; grand, connected

pages.text: There is a catch. The coal and oil buried underground took millions of years to form, and we are using them up fast. They will not last forever, and burning them dirties the air and warms the whole planet. This is one of the great problems your generation will have to solve.

image.note: A smoking chimney beside a nearly-empty fuel gauge; a concerned but not frightening tone

pages.text: The good news is that some energy will never run out. The Sun will shine, the wind will blow and the rivers will flow long after all the coal is gone. Clever people are learning to catch this clean energy with solar panels, wind turbines and dams. Nigeria's strong sun is a treasure that arrives free, every morning.

image.note: Rooftop solar panels catching bright Nigerian sun, a wind turbine turning; hopeful, clean

pages.text: Here is a thought to carry with you. Every beat of your heart, every breath, every step, every idea flickering through your mind, is energy at work. The energy that lets you read this sentence was, a little while ago, sunlight falling on a field where your food grew. You are sunlight, walking around.

image.note: A child glowing gently from within, a faint sun-thread linking them back to a field of crops; poetic

pages.text: So energy is the thread that runs through the whole world. It never vanishes, it only changes shape, and nearly all of it began in the Sun. Learn to see it, and the world stops being a set of separate things and becomes one great, connected, endlessly turning machine, and you are a living part of it.

image.note: A wide warm scene of a busy, sunlit estate, everything in motion, all faintly glowing; closing
